first_principles_point: Healthcare tools are the physical and administrative systems that turn medical need into a test, procedure, prescription, hospital stay, device use, or reimbursed claim.
money_path: patient/payer/provider need -> test/device/hospital/distributor/tool -> delivered event or product -> reimbursement/service/product payment -> working capital/cost structure -> operating cash
company_examples: Abbott; Thermo Fisher; HCA; McKesson; Stryker; Exact Sciences; Labcorp; Quest; Intuitive Surgical
proof_needed: procedure volume; test volume; reimbursement; payer mix; receivables; inventory; device margin; hospital labor; drug-distribution working capital; cash flow
safe_use: Use as a no-background healthcare tools frame, not as proof that medical need automatically becomes cash.

first_principles_point: Healthcare demand matters only after it becomes an actual event: a test run, device implanted, drug delivered, admission staffed, claim coded, and payment collected.
money_path: medical need -> operational event -> bill/claim/invoice -> collection -> cash
company_examples: hospitals; labs; device makers; distributors; suppliers
proof_needed: volume; utilization; denial; receivables; collection; payer mix; cash conversion
safe_use: Safe claim: care infrastructure turns need into billable events.

first_principles_point: Screening growth often comes from lowering participation friction, not only inventing better science.
money_path: at-risk population -> easy test pathway -> test volume -> reimbursement -> lab scale and cash
company_examples: Exact Sciences; Labcorp; Quest; Abbott diagnostics; Thermo Fisher
proof_needed: test volume; reimbursement; screening revenue; payer coverage; lab cost; receivables; FCF
safe_use: Safe claim: easier screening can increase utilization, but utilization is not outcome proof.

first_principles_point: Diagnostics turn uncertainty into a care decision, so they sit before treatment, reimbursement, and follow-on spending.
money_path: symptom/risk -> diagnostic test -> result -> treatment pathway -> payment and follow-on care
company_examples: Abbott; Thermo Fisher; Labcorp; Quest; Exact Sciences
proof_needed: test volume; revenue per test; payer mix; denial rate; lab capacity; turnaround; cash collection
safe_use: Safe claim: diagnostics route care decisions; do not claim better outcomes without clinical evidence.

first_principles_point: Devices turn clinician skill into repeatable procedure capacity, but they depend on hospital budgets, training, approvals, and procedure volume.
money_path: procedure need -> device/implant/system -> hospital purchase/use -> payer payment or hospital budget -> manufacturer margin/cash
company_examples: Stryker; Abbott; Intuitive Surgical; Medtronic as reference; Boston Scientific as reference
proof_needed: procedure volume; device sales; installed base; consumables; segment margin; inventory; recalls
safe_use: Safe claim: devices monetize procedure infrastructure when usage and margin are visible.

first_principles_point: A hospital is a capacity system: beds, staff, equipment, payer contracts, acuity, supply, billing, and collections must all work together.
money_path: patient need -> staffed hospital service -> payer/self-pay bill -> collection -> labor/supply/debt cost -> cash
company_examples: HCA; Tenet; Universal Health Services; surgery centers
proof_needed: admissions; same-facility revenue; payer mix; labor cost; bad debt; acuity; OCF
safe_use: Safe claim: hospitals convert care demand into cash only when staffing, payer mix, and collections work.

old_html_inputs: Gray Wave Dividend; Spread Machine as secondary logic
first_principles_point: Drug distribution is access infrastructure with huge revenue, thin margin, inventory risk, receivables/payables timing, and compliance burden.
money_path: prescription/drug demand -> wholesaler/distributor -> pharmacy/provider/customer -> invoice/payment timing -> working capital/cash
company_examples: McKesson; Cencora; Cardinal Health; CVS/Caremark as reference
proof_needed: revenue; operating profit; inventory; receivables; payables; customer concentration; cash conversion
safe_use: Safe claim: distribution revenue is not margin proof.

first_principles_point: Aging increases demand for procedures, monitoring, drugs, nutrition, home support, diagnostics, and chronic-care infrastructure, but payment and labor still decide cash.
money_path: aging patient need -> tool/site/distributor/provider -> service/product -> payer/reimbursement -> cost and cash
company_examples: Abbott; HCA; McKesson; Stryker; home-care and senior-care references
proof_needed: volume; payer mix; reimbursement; labor; receivables; margin; working capital
safe_use: Safe claim: demographics support demand but do not prove reimbursement or cash quality.

first_principles_point: Healthcare tools sell inside a trust system: safety, quality, regulatory approval, documentation, billing accuracy, and compliance are part of the product.
money_path: clinical/regulatory risk -> approved/trusted tool or process -> provider/payer adoption -> payment -> compliance cost and cash
company_examples: Abbott; Stryker; Thermo Fisher; hospitals; labs; distributors
proof_needed: approvals; recalls; quality issues; compliance cost; denials; retention; margin
safe_use: Safe claim: trust is operational in healthcare; it must be proven through adoption and risk control.

first_principles_point: Healthcare can have demand and still trap cash in inventory, receivables, claims, denials, and payer timing.
money_path: product/service delivered -> receivable/inventory/claim -> collection/payable timing -> operating cash
company_examples: McKesson; HCA; Abbott; Stryker; Thermo Fisher
proof_needed: DSO; inventory; receivables; payables; denial; cash conversion; OCF vs net income
safe_use: Safe claim: cash timing is central in healthcare infrastructure.

first_principles_point: More tests, devices, admissions, or prescriptions do not automatically mean better health outcomes or fairer access.
money_path: medical event -> clinical result -> payer/provider economics -> cash and outcome evidence
proof_needed: clinical evidence; utilization; readmission; quality; reimbursement; patient access; cash
safe_use: Safe claim: this page studies infrastructure and cash routes, not final medical outcomes.

first_principles_point: Each company must be read by the medical event it enables and the payment timing behind that event.
money_path: event type -> volume metric -> reimbursement/pricing metric -> working-capital/cost metric -> cash
company_examples: Abbott; Thermo Fisher; HCA; McKesson; Stryker
proof_needed: organic sales; procedure/test volume; payer mix; inventory; receivables; margin; OCF; FCF
safe_use: Safe claim: company examples are candidates until direct annual-report extraction upgrades them.
